LinkedIn Swindler

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Cape Town man, dubbed the LinkedIn Swindler by his victims, is accused of raking in millions of rand through an international fee stealing scam.

Unique Selling Point:
Evan Török is based in Cape Town, South Africa. But, his tentacles reach far and wide. He is accused of stealing money from people around the world in a sophisticated scam, that has allegedly been in operation since at least 2017. Török fronts the company Oncidium Capital which purports to provide financial capital for projects around the world. Using LinkedIn to contact brokers who act on his behalf to secure clients, he lures people in with the promise that he has billions to invest in their projects. His lawyer, Renel James, added legitimacy to his business, by providing legal letters assuring that he has the money to invest in these multi-million dollar projects. Once he entered into the deal he required a refundable underwriter's fee. Once that is paid, he goes to ground, and the money promised for projects is never paid out.

Summary:
Bryan Harveston is one of his victims. He is a Texan who was first introduced to Evan two years ago. He paid 20,000 US dollars in refundable underwriters fees, with the expectation that Evan would fund his gas and petroleum project of 200 million US dollars. Once the underwriters fees had been paid, Evan communicated less and less, until it became clear that he was scamming Harveston. Harveston wrote about his experiences in a report posted online last year and within weeks he was contacted by dozens of other victims. There are 39 and counting. 22 have provided sworn affidavits. One of them is Douw du Preez who lives in Robertson in the Western Cape, South Africa and lost over R400,000 in underwriters fees. He has opened a case at the Robertson police station, where all the sworn statements from around the world have been submitted.

Further information:
Douw du Preez is one of the most recent victims and entered into a deal with Evan this year. He was no longer operating under the company name Oncidium Capital but rather Hat Capital Partners. Evan's father Janos was found guilty of contravening sections of the Financial Act. He was fined seven million rand two years ago, and barred from working in the financial services industry for ten years. It seems the apple does not fall far from the tree.

Script:


VO 1 Cape Town…its seductive beauty attracts international tourists…but also the criminal elite.

VO 2 ..who often flaunt their ill-gotten gains with seemingly little fear of prosecution.

VO 3 It’s from here that Evan Török has built an international network designed to attract clients from around the world

VO 4 He’s reached far and wide….enriching himself with millions of rand in recent years in an allegedly fraudulent financial scam..

VO 5 His alleged victims call him the LinkedIn Swindler….as he uses the business networking platform to recruit his clients.

UPSOUND Bryan Harveston (Zoom Interview) 02:45 we were seeking about 200 million is what we were seeking but landed on 51 million dollar amount we were going to do with Evan to keep our cost to capital going in low.

VO 6 Bryan Harveston, is from Texas in the U.S., and first met Evan Török, director of Oncidium Capital, online in 2021 while trying to raise money for a gas and petroleum project.

VO 7 Török claimed to have access to the funds and a loan agreement was drawn up, but first Bryan would have to pay an underwriter’s fee.

ERIN: What is an underwriter’s fee, what is it for?

UPSOUND Bryan Harveston (Zoom interview) 07:39 An underwriter’s fee from what we understand is a good faith payment from our side to a source like Evan who is going to be providing his funding services.

VO 8 In other words, to get the loan, clients would first have to pay a fee… in Bryan’s case over 20,000 US dollars.

VO 9 In return, he was supposed to get funding for his multimillion dollar project…. But that never happened.

UPSOUND Bryan Harveston 13:00 Evan was creative, he’d keep the dollar amounts low, that was part of his strategy, so people would spend more money legally trying to pursue him than it would cost to get the money back.

VO 10 39 alleged victims have come forward so far.

UPSOUND Bryan Harveson 24:32 Based on his victims accounts that I’ve uncovered, I consider him a notorious international scammer and he’s been conducting these scams since 2017.

VO 11 But, how is it possible that so many people fell for the scam?

VO 12 Elias Papastamatis, a broker who spoke to us from Sydney, Australia, says Torok knew exactly what to do.

UPSOUND Elias Papastamatis (Zoom interview) Time code: 02:24 He dangled a carrot and that would make the client and ourselves feel comfortable that this was going to go ahead.

VO 13 He’d send voice notes assuring Elias the deals were on track.

VOICE NOTE from Evan “If you’re stressed go and drink something mate” https://freesound.org/peopEle/FraudWatch/ (second last clip towards the end)

VO 14 But, Elias started warning clients of the red flags …. Torok was quick to retaliate.

VOICE NOTE from Evan A legal letter has to go out now unfortunately my friend (slams table), its false information he’s spreading around from unprofessional sources. We are holding on all the transactions now. All the transactions will be held (slams his hand down). (https://freesound.org/people/FraudWatch/ -First voice note on the list)

VO 15 To boost his credibility, Torok relied on this woman: Renel James…who claimed to be independent senior counsel who had seen proof of Toroks funds.

UPSOUND Annette Black (Zoom) 04:57 It was August 2020 and she said she’d been associated with Evan in different legal capacities since 2014. She went on to assure me the funds were there and available.

VO 16 Annette Black, a New Zealand businesswoman was trying to raise 55 million US dollars for an eco aquaculture project. Agreements were signed and she paid the underwriter’s fees of over 4000 US dollars.

UPSOUND Annette Black 09:13 It was going to a foreign exchange company to go to Renel to go to Evan. Which for an underwriting fee is very unusual. 04:35 The transaction, the payments go through Renel so she was obviously part of it.

VO 17 And once the underwriter’s fees were paid, Torok went to ground.

UPSOUND Annette Black - When I started to realise it wasn’t right and I wasn’t getting any answers from him. And i’m talking here about endless days of phone calls and whatsapps, emailing on and on and on. I contacted Renel James. ( Clip 6047 Day Two and Clip 6047. Lots of clips right at beginning of Day 2 of all the documents) (Emails from Annette to Renel)

LINK Clip 6129 / Day 2 We’ve managed to get hold of Renel on whatsapp and she’s agreed to do a phone interview

NATSOUND Phone ringing

VO 18 Renel told us she set up Eros Global Administration, a UK registered business, to help Török process transactions with foreign clients.

UPSOUND: Renel James Clip 6129 / Day Two Time code 01:32 He said could I please set up a company in the UK. which I could. It was very easy for me to facilitate that and then receive the fees and pay them onto him, so I agreed to that.

VO 19 The two were romantically involved for about 18 months, and Renel claims, at first, she believed his deals were above board.

UPSOUND Renel James 04:25 He showed me a letter from a bank, two different banks, addressed to his company, showing access to a lot of cash. But, it wasn’t transaction specific Time code 04:52 off the back of that I confirmed I had seen the funds.

VO 20 But, funds were never paid out, and pressure from clients mounted …when they couldn’t get hold of Török to get their underwriters fees back, they’d contact Renel instead.

UPSOUND Renel James 07:40 By August 2021, when I realised this is becoming a me problem, I dissolved the whole thing with Eros.

VO 21 But, it appears Eros was still operational in November 2021.

VO 21a Renel also ended their relationship that same year.

ERIN: 12:46 What do you think of Evan now after everything that’s happened?
Renel: I don’t want to pass judgement on his character, but had I known that this was going to happen I would have stayed very very far away. 09:57 When I started to become suspicious I exited. 10:06 That is the honest side of my story

VO 22 It was time to get some answers from Evan Török himself.

LINK Day Two Clip 6102 We’re outside what we’ve confirmed is Toroks address in Hout Bay. We’re going to see if we can get his response to these allegations.

NATSOUND Ringing the bell (As per frameio notes let viewer hear him answer)

VO 23 We gave him one more chance to respond. And approached his front door.

NATSOUND Erin knocking, him slamming door / Day Two Clip 6106 Time code 01:53 “These are very serious allegations of you running an international criminal scam. Time code 01:57 That is completely false ma’am. Time code 02:36 I’d love to have a chat with you. (please use subtitles as he is speaking through the door)

VO 24 As it turns out, we didn’t have that chat, but his lawyer did contact us.

UPSOUND AUDIO Clip 6115 / Day Two 01:43 "He's being harrassed a bit for the last couple of weeks so he's nervous.

VO 25 In a statement to Carte Blanche, Török denied any “foul play” in his business dealings.

VO 26 But that’s not the way his alleged victims remember it.

UPSOUND Elias Papastamatis 12:45 My sleep was about two hours a night, and I was chasing, chasing Evan for information about what is happening with our loans.

VO 27 As a broker Elias had provided Torok with dozens of clients - five of them paid underwriter’s fees and never received the loans they were promised.

ERIN: 17:53 on zoom interview And what did you glean about his lifestyle?

UPSOUND: Elias Papastamatis 17:59 Lots of alcohol, cocaine, meeting up with the girls. He’s a womaniser and a drug addict.

LINK: Clip 5971 Day Two We’re on our way to Robertson, a country town in the Western Cape - an unlikely destination for this investigation.

VO 28 It’s a far cry from the world Torok inhabits - it’s a sleepy town, known for its vineyards and winemaking.

VO 29 It’s also where Torok’s latest alleged victim, a South African, lives. He doesn’t want to be identified, so we’ll call him Michael. The answers he provided have been re-recorded with an actor.

VO 30 In April, Michael paid over R400,000 in underwriters fees into the Standard Bank account of Torok’s new business….different name, but same modus operandi.

UPSOUND ‘Michael’ / Anonymous (He is “James” in Zoom interview, but have changed to Michael) (PLEASE BLOCK HIM OUT - if you can do the example I sent you on whatsapp from Netlix doccie) 12:34 “He registered a new company. It’s called Six Capital Partners or Hat Capital Partners and this is the business that he’s is running at the moment. (ACTOR’s Voice, sent on wetransfer)

VO 31 It's here in this country village that the activities of Evan Torok may finally come to an end.

ERIN: (Zoom with Michael) 15:11 Do you think this small town police station is going to bring this international scammer to book?

UPSOUND James 15:18 I think so. I think they will. I think they are on it and I think they will bring justice and it will be really great for our town, and for the people of South Africa. (Please use actor’s voice sent on wetransfer)

VO 32 Michael has filed a case, with 22 sworn statements gathered from victims around the world at the Robertson police station (clip 6025 to clip 6035) (clip 6045)

VO 33 Elias hopes Torok will soon be arrested, and believes Renel James must also be held accountable.

UPSOUND Elias Papstamatis 19:56 I want him to face the music. I want him to spend time in jail. I want his accomplice to do the same. 25:26 I think she was an accomplice in the whole thing. I believe that. And I think he needed her to get loans through.

VO 34 Torok could soon face multiple charges of theft under false pretences.

VO 35 The so called LinkedIn Swindler has allegedly stolen a combined R15 million in underwriters fees from victims who have so far come forward.

VO 36 Robertson police confirmed they’re investigating.

VO 37 For his victims, the investigation is a vindication… the mental anguish for many of them still lingers.

UPSOUND Annette Black (Zoom interview) ime code 15:59 Its absolutely mental cruelty. Because you get a glimmer of hope and then it’s gone. Time code 21:45 Nobody had been able to get their money back. That’s how good he is. He’s made a career of it and its just got to stop.

VO 38 If his guilt is established, the seeds of Torok’s eventual downfall will have been sewn in a quiet corner of the Cape Winelands.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A Cape Town man, dubbed the LinkedIn Swindler by his victims, is accused of raking in millions of rand through an international fee stealing scam.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Evan Török is based in Cape Town, South Africa. But, his tentacles reach far and wide. He is accused of stealing money from people around the world in a sophisticated scam, that has allegedly been in operation since at least 2017. Török fronts the company Oncidium Capital which purports to provide financial capital for projects around the world. Using LinkedIn to contact brokers who act on his behalf to secure clients, he lures people in with the promise that he has billions to invest in their projects. His lawyer, Renel James, added legitimacy to his business, by providing legal letters assuring that he has the money to invest in these multi-million dollar projects. Once he entered into the deal he required a refundable underwriter's fee. Once that is paid, he goes to ground, and the money promised for projects is never paid out.
metadata.Summary: Bryan Harveston is one of his victims. He is a Texan who was first introduced to Evan two years ago. He paid 20,000 US dollars in refundable underwriters fees, with the expectation that Evan would fund his gas and petroleum project of 200 million US dollars. Once the underwriters fees had been paid, Evan communicated less and less, until it became clear that he was scamming Harveston. Harveston wrote about his experiences in a report posted online last year and within weeks he was contacted by dozens of other victims. There are 39 and counting. 22 have provided sworn affidavits. One of them is Douw du Preez who lives in Robertson in the Western Cape, South Africa and lost over R400,000 in underwriters fees. He has opened a case at the Robertson police station, where all the sworn statements from around the world have been submitted.
metadata.Further information: Douw du Preez is one of the most recent victims and entered into a deal with Evan this year. He was no longer operating under the company name Oncidium Capital but rather Hat Capital Partners. Evan's father Janos was found guilty of contravening sections of the Financial Act. He was fined seven million rand two years ago, and barred from working in the financial services industry for ten years. It seems the apple does not fall far from the tree.
